paragraphs.text: 24. Likewise, again, concerning the evil deeds throughout the whole earth.
If everyone goes astray and every mouth speaks lies, must not God remain true? Is it not impossible and inconceivable for him to lie?

If our sins and our lawless deeds had not shaken heaven and earth, what would the sword be doing standing there? Or would it appear drawn, ready to act according to its will, whether it wished to remain outside its sheath or did not wish to return?
Not because it was satisfied, but because it had yielded to the will of the man who stood beside it. [?]

Or what kind of sword is it, and what is its sheath, or what covers it? What are its length and breadth, and how is it stretched out? Or what is its light, or what are the places where it has appeared?
Or the person beside whom it stretched upward will not tell it,
or, even if he tells it, he will tell it in another way.

Do not think that the sword whose forms and appearance it is a blessing to see is like the sword about which the prophet spoke, it: “Sword, sword, be sharp and rage, so that you may slaughter victims! Be sharp so that you may flash!”
ready to destroy them utterly. Strike, despise it, and cast away every tree.”
This, indeed, is given into the hand of the one who will slaughter.
But this sword itself is in control.

as it is said, “The sword has been sharpened and is ready to be put into the hand of the one who will slaughter.” This sword, however, holds the man, and the man is at its disposal. It slaughters through the man those whom it slaughters; the man does not slaughter with it. It is not the person who turns it toward the place where he wants to slaughter. Rather, it is the sword itself that turns the person toward the place where it wants to slaughter.
It is not the person who takes revenge with it in anger. Rather, it is the sword itself that uses the person to take revenge on those with whom it is angry,

For the man is in its hands, while it is not in the man’s hands. It is the one that always delivers those whom it slaughters into the hands of the one who is in its hands, as a holy man says, “They will be delivered into the hand of the sword.”

Just as this sword was urged through the prophet to become sharp according to the Lord’s command, “Sword, sword, be sharpened for wrath,” it was also rebuked so that it would turn back from the place where it was slaughtering.

Indeed, another judgment came upon it, so that it would be judged, or vengeance would be taken on it after it had taken vengeance on those whom it slaughtered, as the word says: “Turn back; do not remain in the place where you were born. I will judge you in your land.”
Was it not the Lord who told it to carry out strikes?

Why, again, did he say, after it had finished being directed against bones—and it was directed toward destruction—“I will [?] judge you. [?] pour out my wrath upon you and kindle a fire against you in my anger”?
and hand you over to barbarous people who bring about destruction. You will become fuel for the fire, and your blood will be in the midst of your land.
You will no longer be remembered”?
This is not the occasion or the time to speak about these things,

But against you instead, in a portion of this kind, or of what belongs to the sword that revealed itself as a testimony against those who commit these abominations among us, nor [?] is there anyone who tells it, “Slaughter,” nor is there anyone who tells it, “Stop slaughtering.”

It has the authority to strike or not to strike. It is not given orders; rather, it itself gives orders. It is not under the authority of the one who strikes. Instead, the one who strikes with it is under its authority. It obeys God alone.
It is not drawn out of its sheath by someone else. It draws itself out of its sheath and returns itself to its sheath.
It did not come out of its sheath to slaughter until its anger was exhausted, as the Lord said about it: “It is directed toward destruction.”
Or: “I have drawn my sword out of its sheath, and it will not return to it from now on.”
Or: “They have been handed over to the sword to slaughter them at every gate.”
It has been properly prepared to slaughter; it has been properly made to flash like lightning.
“Sword, move and be sharpened to the right and to the left, wherever your face is turned.”
It was said to this sword, “I will judge you in your land.” Yet the whole earth will be judged through it, and everyone will be judged by means of it.
A blessing and a curse, wrath and mercy, are on its two faces, one on this side and one on that, as it flashes with righteous judgment.
Because of it, God pours out his anger on those who provoke him with their wicked deeds.
Because of it, he also turns away from his anger.
Its coming down in its sheath is grace.
Its returning to him is glory.
It is terrifying to see it drawn.
It is a joy to see it returning to its sheath, as are, in truth, the things involved in its stretching out to slaughter.
Peace is what is involved in its turning back from the places where it slaughters those whom it pierces.
Strength is what is in its handle.
Firmness is what is in its blade.
Compassion, mercy, kindness, cheerfulness, and hope for every good thing are what is in its preparation, or its entire disposition.
But it is also stripped of these.
And these are what its sheath consists of, together with all the other things of this kind.
Its covering and its sheath belong to the Hidden One. Faith is what is in its mystery.
The sun's coming up in its place, before it rises high or spreads out, is what is in its unveiling, because no one can bear the rays of its light.

Patience and restraint are present in its revelation. It did not reveal itself to take vengeance in the places where it stood, lest it slaughter innocent people along with sinners, but rather to hand over those who sinned in those places to vengeance in the days of vengeance, about which the Lord said in the Gospel, “For these are the days of vengeance.”

No sword can move from a place unless it is moved by those who have authority. But this sword not only has authority from within itself to go to the place where it wants to go, but also to carry the person through whom it slaughters, or who slaughters with it, moving him from the places where he is to other places.
It also brings it back from the places to which it takes it, leaving it in its own places.

What is within it is not a spirit of life like that of the living creatures above whom is the glory of the God of Israel, according to what the prophet said about the wheels moving beneath him: “A spirit of life is within them.”
Rather, it is itself life in its entirety, and every spirit of life exists through it.
Knowledge and the Word are its strength. Love is what is in its adornment or its beauty.
God alone, the Almighty, is its height and its breadth, which cannot be measured. For if it wants to rise higher, it rises.
Likewise, if it wants to spread out, it spreads out. If it wants to contract, it contracts. If it wants to become low, it becomes low, without revealing itself according to its dimensions.

For its entire preparation has no measure. Instead, it reveals itself according to the capacity of those who can bear to see it, in the places where it slaughters and which it heals, because it strikes;
But it also heals.
it wounds and treats those whom it strikes because of their disobedience.
It also terrifies those whom the enemy has weakened with his arrows.

Its handle, or the place where it is held, is the light of the eyes of those who look toward uprightness, truth, and every act of devotion to God. The places into which it draws near or in which it hangs are the Scriptures or the laws that were given so that we might be saved through them.
As for us humans, the storehouses in which it always lies are the heavens of heavens, while humans are in its hands like these stones.
Or he is nothing before it when it is in a person's hands, to the extent that he can pierce with it.
Its sharpness comes from within it. It is not sharpened by others, as every other sword is sharpened. Rather, its sharpness comes from within it; it is in the person who seeks it.
If it is not revealed, he does not see it.
It draws near to the person who seeks it.
But also far removed from it.
In it they said this: “The word of God is living

And it is active and cuts more sharply than any double-edged sword. Through it the command was given in this way for Christ’s soldiers to take the helmet of salvation and the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God, so that we might be strong in battle, striking down with it those who oppose them, as the strong were instructed.
